key_points: GDPNow jumped to 4.3% for Q3, signalling re-accelerating activity driven by AI capex and resilient consumption; FOMC describes growth as solid.
Consumer sentiment rebounded from 49.5 to 55.2, low claims (209k) and unemployment down to 4.1% offset a flat July payroll print.
Strong growth plus elevated inflation and hawkish dissents argue for modest upward pressure on yields, especially at the long end via term premium, keeping a mild steepening bias.

Growth momentum and earnings support equities and tight credit spreads, though spreads at 3rd percentile and VIX at 3rd percentile limit further compression and favor mild mean reversion over 3 months.
US growth outperformance vs. weaker Europe/Canada gives a slight dollar-supportive tilt; commodity and gold views roughly neutral from a growth lens.
July CPI rose only about 0.08% m/m, and June core PCE rose about 0.13% m/m. Monthly inflation momentum is clearly cooling even though year-over-year rates remain about 3.3%.

Soft prints undercut the case of the three hawkish dissenters (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan), who wanted a hike. That biases the 2y modestly lower and favors further 2s10s steepening as hike pricing fades.

The 10y at the 97th percentile of its 1y range is driven more by term premium than by inflation compensation. The 10y breakeven of 2.27 is at the 30th percentile and anchored, so there is only a mild downside bias for the 10y from the inflation lens.

Oil rebounded 5% this week to $84 after falling from the $114 Hormuz peak. This gives a mild upward pull on near-term breakevens, but the staff expects headline inflation to slow in 2H as gasoline declines.

Disinflationary relief supports equities and gold and weighs slightly on the dollar. However, the HY spread and VIX sit at the 3rd percentile of their ranges, leaving asymmetric upside risk if inflation re-accelerates.

Labor signals are mixed: July payrolls -23k (soft headline) but unemployment fell to 4.1% and claims remain very low at ~209k, consistent with low-hire/low-fire and constrained labor supply rather than deterioration.

Low claims and falling unemployment remove the labor case for Fed cuts; with three dissents for a hike, labor data does not push the Fed dovish, but negative payrolls cap the hawkish case — net near-neutral for front-end yields.
Fed views wage growth (~3.4% AHE) as consistent with disinflation, so labor is not an inflation driver; little labor-driven edge for breakevens or the dollar.

Stable labor market supports earnings and risk assets near term, but HY spreads and VIX at 1y extremes leave asymmetric room for a widening/vol pickup if the early-September jobs report confirms payroll weakness.
Key event inside the 1m horizon is the August employment report; a second negative payroll print would steepen the curve via lower 2y yields.
Fed on hold at 3.50-3.75% with a hawkish tilt: easing bias dropped in June, three dissents for a hike in July, and 'will deliver price stability' language.
The 2y at 4.17% sits ~55bp above the effective funds rate, so roughly two hikes are already priced; the hawkish path is largely in the price.
July minutes on Aug 19 likely read hawkish, a modest near-term upside risk for front-end yields.
Softer data (July payrolls -23k, CPI +0.08% m/m) argue against additional hike pricing building into the September SEP; front-end is skewed slightly lower over 3m.
Term premium and a shift to price-sensitive Treasury holders keep the 10y supported near 1y highs, which favours gradual 2s10s steepening.
Dollar has limited upside from rate differentials because the ECB and BoE are also hiking or signalling hikes.

Easy financial conditions (NFCI -0.55, HY spreads at 3rd percentile, VIX at 3rd percentile) support equities, but tight spreads and low vol leave asymmetric upside for spreads and VIX over longer horizons.

Term premium is the driver: the 10y rose ~50bp since the Middle East conflict began and sits at the 97th percentile of its 1y range, while the 2y is flat over the month — a classic supply/term-premium bear steepening.
The Desk notes the ownership shift from price-insensitive official holders to price-sensitive private investors, which structurally raises the term premium needed to absorb heavy coupon issuance.

Fed reserve-management bill purchases and reinvestment of agency MBS into bills shrink the bill supply and anchor the front end, so the 2y lags while long-end supply pressure supports 2s10s steepening.

With the August refunding and its auctions behind us, there is no major supply catalyst near term, so the 1w edge is small; the September quarter-end, fiscal-year-end TGA dynamics and refunding into November keep a modest upward bias for long yields over 1-3m.
Speculators are already very short 10y futures (9th percentile), which caps conviction on further 10y upside and argues for steepener exposure rather than an outright bear position.
Fiscal and debt-supply concerns modestly support gold and weigh slightly on the dollar, since yields driven by term premium rather than policy rates are less dollar-positive.
HY spreads and the VIX near the 3rd percentile are vulnerable if long yields rise further, so a mild upward tilt for both at the 1-3m horizons.
Liquidity is ample: Fed balance sheet growing again via reserve management bill purchases (WALCL +$11bn w/w, +$119bn y/y), repo trading below IORB, ON RRP take-up modest — no funding stress.

Financial conditions very loose: NFCI -0.55, HY OAS 2.67% at 3rd percentile of 1y range, VIX 14.25 at 3rd percentile — supportive for equities near-term but leaves little room for further compression, so spreads and VIX skew modestly upward over 1-3m.
Private credit softening (BDC outflows, redemptions) is a slow-burn tail risk for spreads rather than an immediate catalyst.

Hawkish Fed (3 dissents for a hike) with loose conditions creates upside risk for the front end, but the liquidity lens offers little directional edge on yields or the dollar; dollar sits low in its range with crowded long DX spec positioning.
Equity drift favored by abundant liquidity and strong earnings/AI capex, tempered by record-high level and extreme ES long positioning.
10y T-note specs very short (9th pct of 52w) with yields at 97th pct of range; short covering already started (+64k), contrarian lean toward lower 10y yields and a flatter 2s10s.
2y futures positioning is the least short of the year (97th pct), so no crowding signal at the front end; near-neutral 2y view.
Dollar index specs crowded long (97th pct) while the broad dollar sits near the low of its range: contrarian modest downside for DTWEXBGS.

Complacency cluster: ES net long at 99th pct, VIX at 3rd pct, HY OAS at 3rd pct of range — trend supports equities but upside is crowded; spreads and VIX skewed to mean-revert higher over 1-3 months, especially into September seasonality.
Gold specs adding longs (74th pct) despite price at 17th pct of range — mild positive; crude positioning neutral (43rd pct) after a 5% weekly bounce, no edge.

Foreign central banks (ECB hiking, UK hikes priced) are hawkish while the Fed holds at 3.50-3.75%; narrowing short-rate differentials and a dollar already down 1.3% over 1m lean against the broad dollar.
Speculative DX longs at the 97th percentile (43% of open interest) are crowded, adding unwind risk to the dollar downside.

Global term premium pressure (foreign yields rising, shift from price-insensitive official holders to private investors) supports higher US 10y and a steeper 2s10s, while 2y is anchored by a Fed on hold.
A softer dollar and strong Asian high-tech/AI exports support S&P 500 earnings and gold; gold has spec length building from the 17th percentile of its 1y range.
Weaker growth in Europe, Canada, Mexico and lower-income Asia from energy costs caps oil upside after the 5% weekly bounce; Hormuz reopening reduces the supply premium.
VIX and HY spreads at 3rd-percentile lows leave asymmetric risk to wider/higher over 1-3 months from global shocks (Middle East, foreign slowdown).

WTI at $84 is down ~20% over 3 months after the US-Iran MoU and Hormuz reopening, but bounced 5% last week; normalizing Gulf supply argues for a modest downward drift over 1-3 months, with tail risk from conflict re-escalation.
Spec crude length is mid-range (43rd pct) and fell last week, so positioning gives no strong squeeze signal either way.
Breakevens (2.27%, 30th pct) track oil; with energy pass-through expected to fade in H2 per staff outlook, slight downside bias for T10YIE at 3m.
Lower energy prices ease headline inflation, marginally reducing pressure on front-end yields despite three hawkish dissents; 10y term premium stays elevated, mild steepening bias.
Gold near the bottom of its 1y range with rising spec length and rebounding momentum; slight upside tilt.
VIX at 3rd percentile and HY spreads at 3rd percentile leave asymmetric risk of mean reversion higher, especially if Middle East supply shocks re-emerge.
Cheaper energy and strong AI capex support equities; S&P near record highs with normal positive drift.

Middle East conflict and Hormuz disruption drove oil from about 115 down toward 55 after the US-Iran MoU; the +5.3% weekly rebound to 84 hints that the geopolitical risk premium is not dead, which keeps two-way oil risk high.
VIX at its 3rd percentile and HY spreads at their 3rd percentile price almost no geopolitical or political tail risk; the asymmetry favors higher VIX and wider spreads, especially over 3m.

US midterm elections (early November) fall inside the 3m window; pre-election uncertainty in October typically lifts implied volatility and supports curve steepening via fiscal and term-premium concerns.
Gold sits near the low end of its 1y range with speculators adding longs; it is a cheap geopolitical hedge, so I lean modestly bullish.

Tariff pass-through and energy shocks keep inflation risk skewed up, but a geopolitical flare would also bring flight-to-quality, so the effects on 10y yields and the dollar roughly offset; front-end yields lean slightly lower on risk-off and on the Fed's reluctance to hike into shocks.
Equity momentum and AI capex remain strong, so the S&P keeps a slight positive drift despite stretched levels.

thesis:
The Fed is on hold at 3.50-3.75% with a hawkish tilt: three dissents favored a hike and the easing bias was dropped. The 2y at 4.17% already prices roughly two hikes, while recent data are softer (July CPI +0.08% m/m, payrolls -23k), so I lean slightly lower on the front end over 1-3 months and expect a modest 2s10s steepening.

The 10y sits at the 97th percentile of its 1-year range on term premium. That is balanced by very short spec positioning in 10y futures (9th percentile), with short covering already starting, so the 10y is roughly a coin flip.

The dollar leans mildly weaker: foreign central banks are hiking, short-rate differentials are narrowing and spec DX length is crowded.

Equities keep a positive drift on AI capex, GDPNow at 4.3% and loose financial conditions. Positioning is stretched (ES net long at the 99th percentile), so I don't push beyond about 0.58.

The complacency cluster argues for mean reversion over 1-3 months, with modestly wider credit spreads and a higher VIX. HY OAS and the VIX both sit at the 3rd percentile of their ranges. September seasonality, the September SEP and the November midterms all fall inside the window.

Oil drifts slightly lower as Hormuz supply normalizes and growth abroad is weak, though re-escalation risk keeps this near 0.5. Gold gets a mild upside tilt: it sits near the bottom of its range, spec length is building and the dollar is softer.

Breakevens are anchored and track oil, so I see no edge there.
